name: Ommen

anatomy.part: bow of the hull, the left point
keel, the lowest point of the hull's bowl
stern tip of the hull, the right point
mast foot on the deck, where the mast stands in the hull
sail foot, where the sail meets the mast and the lantern rope leaves it
top of the mast, the yard of the sail
full belly of the sail, bulging out from the mast
masthead lantern at the top of the staff, where the streamer starts
upper prong of the forked streamer
lower prong of the forked streamer

third lantern on the rope, at the rope's upward turn
far end of the lantern rope, the last name said

myth: When the string was cut, the drowned began going aloft by sea, and the sea would not give them back. Kael casts for them every night and never catches one. So Ommen was made: a boat that carries the names. On the night of the drowning, each name said at the harbour mouth is lit, one lantern for each, and the boat sails out along the Leeward Reach with its lamps trailing behind on a rope. Tavo came down cold that year and tore the sails, and laughed, and the boat went on anyway, because Hesk had counted every name and would not lose one. My mother's brother is up there, third lamp from the stern. In hard southern weather, look for the mast. If it is lit, someone is being remembered. If it is dark, go down to the harbour and say a name, so the boat has something to carry.
verse:
Lamps on a wet rope
each name said at the harbour
the boat counts us home
